paragraphs: I am Kai Ming, a game designer obsessed with how systems work. Currently in my third year at DigiPen Institute of Technology Singapore, I’ve moved from making games that 'just work' to designing games that 'feel right.'

I specialise in C# Scripting and UI/UX Prototyping. I love the challenge of taking complex data like an RPG inventory or a strategy game’s HUD, and distilling it into a clean, accessible interface. I’m a firm believer that good UX is invisible; it allows the player to stay immersed in the world I've built.
Currently looking for Internship opportunities where I can break (and then fix) complex problems.

paragraphs: MyTransport.SG is a mobile application developed by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) of Singapore. It provides real-time transport information, including bus arrival times, traffic conditions, parking availability, and journey planning. The app is primarily aimed at daily commuters, drivers, and tourists, offering a one-stop solution for navigating the island's public transport network.

In this study, I will focus on evaluating the app's navigation structure, information clarity, and accessibility features, particularly for elderly users and those with limited familiarity with transport-related terminology. By conducting a heuristic evaluation, user research, and competitive analysis, I aim to identify key design improvements that enhance the app’s usability and overall user experience. UX Evaluation Focus

paragraphs: I began by conducting a Heuristic Evaluation of the existing MyTransport.SG app to identify usability gaps. To ground my design in reality, I developed a User Persona and Empathy Map based on a Chosen User Demographic, allowing me to draft a specific User Story that addressed real-world commuting frustrations. This phase concluded with a User Feedback Analysis, where I synthesised pain points into a clear strategic direction for the redesign.

paragraphs: InNav is an indoor navigation system designed to help users navigate complex multi-storey buildings, such as educational institutions, offices, and public facilities. Unlike conventional navigation applications that primarily focus on outdoor routes, InNav aims to bridge the gap between outdoor and indoor navigation by providing intuitive wayfinding across rooms, corridors, and multiple floors.

The project consists of two main components: an Environment Editor, which allows building layouts to be created and configured, and a Navigation Runtime, which enables users to explore indoor environments and find routes to their destinations. Developed using Unreal Engine 5, the system is designed to be flexible and adaptable to different buildings, with future plans to explore augmented reality (AR) navigation.

As an ongoing team project, my focus is on project management, user experience design, product planning, and coordinating development to ensure the system remains intuitive, accessible, and technically feasible.

paragraphs: I began by identifying the challenges of navigating unfamiliar indoor environments, particularly in large, multi-storey buildings. Working with my team, I helped establish the project's problem statement, target audiences, and core objectives. We focused on the needs of students, visitors, and staff, identifying common difficulties such as locating specific rooms and navigating between floors. These findings guided our product requirements and helped define InNav as a flexible indoor navigation system adaptable to different buildings.

I engineered a scalable architecture to manage the "one-more-run" gameplay loop, integrating a robust multi-slot save/load engine with a decoupled, event-driven achievement and unlock system. paragraphs: Pirate’s Pocket puts you in the boots of a rogue captain on the high seas. Your goal is simple: collect the most treasure. The execution is anything but. By combining strategic hand management with a dynamic "Shield & Parry" defence system, players must decide when to play it safe and when to risk their last doubloon on a desperate dice roll. It’s a game of calculated risks, sudden betrayals, and the constant hunt for the ultimate haul.
